To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the development of agricultural societies in the Central Plains region of China was a key factor that enabled people to adapt to the aridification of the climate during the Neolithic to Bronze Age transition.

1) the CPC experienced a wet climate from 9200–4000 cal BP; 2) the climate changed to a dry condition after 4000 calBP; 3) the CPC experienced four episodes of population growth, and; 4) these episodes are synchronous to the vegetation changes.
the arid climate during the early Bronze Age in the CPC did not cause the collapse of the prehistoric civilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social resilience of the CPC, and the relationship between the population increase and the aridification of the CPC.
the relationship between climate, vegetation and human population in the CPC, and provides new evidence to understand the social resilience of prehistoric societies in the CPC.
the social resilience of the prehistoric CPC, which may be a model for understanding the relationship between climate change and social development in the past.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social resilience in the CPC was the result of the interaction between the environment and the human society.

the CPC was a center of population increase during the Neolithic, which was not a result of the aridification of the climate, but was a result of a social system of agriculture that was able to adapt to a drier climate.

the social resilience to climate variability in the CPC is not only the ability to maintain a population in a stable state in the face of environmental change, but also the ability to recover quickly after a disturbance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social resilience in the CPC during the early Bronze Age was not only due to climate changes, but also the result of the complex interactions of human activities and climate.
the climate change in the CPC was not the primary factor for the collapse of Neolithic civilization.
the climate change did not cause the collapse of the Neolithic society in the CPC, but it did contribute to the development of agriculture, and thus, the development of complex society.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CPC is an important case study to understand the relationship between social resilience and the development of complex societies.
the CPC was a region where human population was not limited by the environment, which may explain the rapid population growth in the CPC during the Bronze Age.
social resilience, rather than climate change, played a key role in shaping the development of the CPC.
